question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f$ as the composite function

$$
f={4}^{u},\,u=-7{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}={4}^{u}\ln(4),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-14x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={4}^{u}\ln(4)\cdot (-14x) \\ & =(-14x)\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4) \\ & =-14x\cdot {4}^{-7{x}^{2}}\ln(4).\end{aligned}
$$
